problem: Classification of Finite Simple Groups (announced c. 1983, quasithin gap closed by Aschbacher–Smith 2004): formal machine-checked proof
result: Claimed complete, sorry-free Lean 4 formalization of the first-generation CFSG proof against TauCeti's statement, plus a repaired step in one published route to the Unbalanced Group Theorem
human_role: AI agents formalized the literature from a human-written blueprint; about 34 named mathematicians and engineers; experts Lyons and Solomon consulted
verification: Lean 4 kernel check claimed by the team (sorry-free, standard axioms); not yet independently rebuilt or audited

problem: Order of growth of the maximal Banach–Mazur distance R∞(n) from n-dimensional normed spaces to the cube ℓ∞ⁿ (Grünbaum's problem)
result: R∞(n) ≥ c·n^{2/3}(log 2n)^{−10}; with the Friedland–Naor–Youssef upper bound, R∞(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}
human_role: Human-led: the author designed the strategy and stated the key proposition; GPT-6 generated its proof, which the author reworked
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Morgan–Mullen conjecture (1996): existence of a primitive completely normal element in every finite field extension; Hachenberger's lower bound
result: Claimed full confirmation of Morgan–Mullen (case n > q new, n ≤ q by Garefalakis–Kapetanakis) and of Hachenberger's bound for all (q, n)
human_role: AI-generated arguments, text, code and Lean under the author's direction; the author checked the proof by hand and the formal statements
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; Lean 4 formalization of the new case (with two cited results as axioms and compiler-trusted computation)

problem: Upper bound for the four-colour triangle Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3) = R₄(3)
result: R(3,3,3,3) ≤ 61 (previous upper bound 62 from 2004; lower bound 51)
ai_system: GPT-5.6 (Codex); Fable 5 (Claude Code); GPT-6 Pro; GPT-6 Astra (Codex)
human_role: Human-led computer-assisted proof; AI coding agents and models contributed reductions, the C case, experiments, formalization and editing
verification: Lean 4 formalization of the reductions plus SAT refutations by two independent solvers (the SAT part is outside Lean); unrefereed preprint with a public reproduction package

problem: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture (1991) in all dimensions; consequences: Bochner–Riesz, Stein's restriction conjecture (interior of range), Kakeya maximal and set conjectures in ℝⁿ
result: Claimed proof of local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation in every dimension n ≥ 2 with ε loss, with Bochner–Riesz, restriction in the interior of the range, Nikodym/Kakeya maximal bounds and full Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets as corollaries
human_role: Credited to 'OpenAI'; released as 'model output directly', with no named human authors and no designated reviewers
verification: Unrefereed manuscript; OpenAI lists Lean comparator statements for the main estimate and the corollaries (not checked by us); no expert assessment yet

problem: Golomb–Welch conjecture (c. 1968–1970): no perfect r-error-correcting Lee code in ℤⁿ for n ≥ 3, r ≥ 2
result: Claimed full proof, in both the lattice and the arbitrary-centre forms
human_role: AI-assisted: authors used ChatGPT to explore proof strategies and check calculations; the authors say they wrote all results and proofs
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprints (2610.33983, 2610.34291); no formalization

problem: Propeller conjecture (Khot–Naor 2008)
result: OpenAI's every-dimension proof (Lean comparator statement) simplified by an expert, with equality cases characterised and the 3D computer search removed
human_role: OpenAI model produced the original proof; Heilman (a prior contributor to the problem) rewrote and improved it, using GPT-6 for manuscript preparation
verification: Lean comparator statement in OpenAI's repository; independent human proof posted on arXiv (unrefereed)

problem: Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions (and her derivative conjecture)
result: Disproved for every even n ≥ 8 (derivative conjecture for even n ≥ 10) with an explicit quartic counterexample
human_role: Agents found the counterexamples and proofs during an olympiad; humans checked every statement and formalized two key equations in Lean
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; partial Lean 4 formalization (Eq. 4.2, 4.7)

problem: Lower tail of triangle counts in sparse G(n,p); conjecture of Yufei Zhao and open problem of Janson–Warnke
result: Variational problem solved for every η ∈ (0,1): minimizers are constant or balanced two-block graphons, with a first-order transition at η* = 0.009217…
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol
human_role: AI-assisted: authors expected the answer from Zhao's work; GPT-6 Astra suggested key proof strategies, Claude helped with the computer-assisted proof, models wrote parts of the verification code and Lean
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint with validated numerics and a Lean 4 formalization

problem: Constructing a solution of the two-dimensional KPZ equation at criticality
result: Construction of the Critical 2D KPZ Process as the unique limit of centred log partition functions of critical 2D directed polymers, a functional of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow; proved non-Gaussian.
human_role: Human-led with substantial AI input: authors supplied structure, literature and judgement; ChatGPT developed key estimates and proofs, some of which failed audit
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2610.31614, ~80 pages plus appendices); checked by its eleven authors

problem: Barry Simon's multidimensional L² conjecture (Problem 8, 'Schrödinger operators in the twenty-first century')
result: False in every dimension d ≥ 2: smooth, bounded, nonnegative, arbitrarily small potentials satisfying the (even weighted) L² condition for which −Δ + V has only pure point spectrum on (0, ∞).
human_role: AI-assisted: authors chose the problem and suspected falsity; ChatGPT developed the construction and the extension to the full spectrum; authors rewrote the argument
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2610.31637); checked by its authors

problem: Asymptotics of the Archimedean local height pairing in degenerations without assuming the Hodge conjecture
result: Removes the Hodge-conjecture hypothesis (and minor hypotheses such as reduced simple normal crossing fibres) from the author's asymptotic formula h(t) − ⟨W,Z⟩ log|t| = O(1)
human_role: AI outlined the argument and found a related p-adic theorem of Scholl; the author worked out the remaining details and wrote the paper, at his advisor's suggestion to try AI
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Nagata's conjecture on plane curves (1959)
result: For r ≥ 10 very general points in P², every nonzero curve of degree d with multiplicities m_i satisfies Σ m_i < d√r (claimed by OpenAI; reorganized and re-proved by Tevelev).
human_role: Autonomous AI proof (OpenAI release, no human author); Tevelev re-derived, simplified and presented it, using ChatGPT Astra only for editing and figures
verification: Re-proved in reorganized form by a named independent specialist (Jenia Tevelev, arXiv 2610.30050, presented in a UMass Amherst talk); unrefereed

problem: Barnette's conjecture (Hamiltonicity of cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graphs)
result: Every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle; indeed G − e is Hamiltonian for every edge e (claimed by OpenAI; written out and partly re-proved by Li).
human_role: Autonomous AI proof (OpenAI release); Zhentao Li re-derived it by hand with combinatorial replacements, using LLMs to read the preprint and format the note
verification: Lean formalization by OpenAI (statement not independently reviewed by us); re-proved in digested form by a named independent graph theorist (arXiv 2610.30490); unrefereed

problem: Hochster's small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture (1973), domain form in equal characteristic zero; Eisenbud–Schreyer–Weyman Ulrich question (2003)
result: A 3-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over C with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module (OpenAI); Anghel extends the obstruction to all dimensions ≥ 3.
human_role: Counterexample autonomous (OpenAI release), building on human preprints by Anghel, Lopez and Chen; Anghel's survey re-proves and generalizes it, with proofs drafted with ChatGPT and Claude
verification: Complete proof given in a survey by a named specialist (Anghel, arXiv 2610.30027), not independent of AI drafting; Lean scope note from OpenAI; nothing refereed

problem: Double-cap conjecture / Witsenhausen's problem on spherical sets without orthogonal pairs
result: For n ≥ 3, sets in S^(n−1) with no orthogonal pair have measure at most that of two opposite caps of radius π/4, with equality only for double caps (claimed)
human_role: Human-led paper with an assistive AI role; the separate Lean proof was produced almost entirely with AI-assisted tools
verification: Unrefereed preprint; separate Lean 4 proof (different argument) with Comparator and two kernels, statements written by the authors, self-assessed

problem: Linear MDS conjecture (Segre 1955; maximum length of MDS codes / arcs), even characteristic
result: For q even and 2 ≤ k ≤ q, the maximum length of a k-dimensional linear MDS code over F_q is q + 1, or q + 2 when k ∈ {3, q − 1}
human_role: Human-led with AI tools: Kumar devised the argument and Claude helped formalize it in Lean; Chen and Huang used ChatGPT to explore proof strategies and check calculations
verification: Lean 4 proof (Mathlib, Comparator, three kernels) registered on Palomar; the Challenge statement adds two definitions (HasMinimumDistance, IsMDS) and was written by the AI agent; arXiv preprint unrefereed

problem: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture: χ ≤ max{ω, Δ − 1} for Δ ≥ 9
result: Claimed proof for all graphs with Δ ≥ 4583, lowering the explicit threshold from 5.3 × 10⁶; the range 9 ≤ Δ < 4583 remains open
human_role: Human-led with AI assistance on specific estimates, parameter optimisation and constructions (author's declaration)
verification: Unrefereed Zenodo preprint; rational-arithmetic checks with published code; not peer-reviewed or formalised

problem: Gale's conjecture (1953) on partitions of 3D sets into four parts of smaller diameter
result: A 101-point set in R³ whose every 4-partition has a part of diameter > 0.88928·diam, exceeding the sphere's 0.88807; first counterexample below dimension 9.
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GigaEvo (DeepSeek 4; Qwen 3 Max; Gemini 3; Claude Opus 4.6)
human_role: Human-led search; GPT-6 Astra co-developed the algorithms and heuristics (some proposed by the AI) that found the set
verification: Explicit finite object checkable in exact integer arithmetic (coordinates in Appendix A, verification scripts in the repository); unrefereed, no Lean

problem: Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture: k-sunflower-free families in 2^[n] have size at most c_k^n with c_k < 2
result: Claimed proof for every k ≥ 3, with the bound 2^((1 − 1/(16k³))n), via a new polynomial-method bound for vector sunflowers.
human_role: AI-assisted: the authors posed the generalization of Naslund–Sawin and rewrote the argument; ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro found the proof of the key Theorem 2
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; authors checked all results; the stated Lean 4.35 proof is not public yet (promised for Palomar)

problem: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture (2-quasitraces / AW*-factors) and the monotone completeness conjecture for AW*-algebras
result: Counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture (from an unreleased OpenAI model, reproduced with a modified construction) and a finite AW*-factor that is not monotone complete
human_role: OpenAI model produced the original quasitrace counterexample; Arulseelan and Hanson re-derived it, devised the monotone completeness argument, and reworked GPT 6 Astra's preliminary write-up
verification: Quasitrace disproof reproduced by named independent experts in an unrefereed preprint; monotone completeness result unrefereed

problem: Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative C*-algebras (Davidson–Kennedy Question 8.4 setting)
result: Claimed commutative counterexamples, including a finite-dimensional one of affine dimension ≤ 129.
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; Codex; GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5
human_role: AI-assisted: human found the first example; GPT-6 Astra developed its initial proof and proposed the finite-dimensional example
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Irrationality exponent of the lemniscate period Ω = Γ(1/4)²/(2√(2π))
result: Claimed proof that the irrationality exponent of Ω equals 2, with a complete Lean 4 development.
human_role: Human-led with AI: Chudnovsky with ChatGPT for exposition and formalization, adapting OpenAI's AI-generated π method
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; complete Lean 4 proof in ancillary files, statement written by the author, built on OpenAI's unreviewed library

problem: Neumann–Zagier conjecture (1985) on tree lattices isometric to Z^n
result: Every positive definite tree lattice has an irreducible vertex; hence a tree presenting Z^n has a vertex of weight one
human_role: AI-assisted: Issa obtained the first proof of Theorem 1.1 with the two models; the authors digested, simplified and strengthened it and wrote the paper themselves
verification: Unrefereed preprint by named experts who checked and re-derived the AI argument

problem: n-queens constant bounds; sharpness of the Cohn–Elkies LP bound; Tuza's conjecture special cases; packing records
result: Claimed 120 records from an autonomous agent, including an ~84× narrower n-queens interval and certified non-sharpness of the Cohn–Elkies bound in dimensions 10 and 11
human_role: Agent-driven campaigns with human-set budgets and starting points from published methods; fixed verifier; humans wrote the report
verification: Unrefereed technical report with public certificates (dual vectors, witnesses); not independently checked

problem: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for H = P_t (induced paths), open beyond P5
result: Claimed proof that every path P_t (and the subdivided claws S_{1,2,t}) has the Erdős–Hajnal property; DeepMind's model and a Claude-assisted manuscript claim the P_t case independently.
ai_system: ChatGPT-6 Astra; Google DeepMind internal model; Claude Opus 5.5
human_role: Human-led (Nguyen): the author's framework, with Astra proving parts of key lemmas; DeepMind's and the Claude manuscripts are described as AI-generated
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; DeepMind's P6 proof verified by Joonkyung Lee with Lean (not yet public); the Claude manuscripts have Lean code but no expert review, and Zhou's Lean theorem is conditional

problem: Is every word-hyperbolic group sofic? (Hyperbolic groups were the leading candidates for sofic counterexamples after residual finiteness)
result: Claimed construction of a torsion-free two-dimensional word-hyperbolic group that is not sofic; independently, a claimed proof with Lean that OpenAI's non-residually-finite hyperbolic group is not sofic.
human_role: AI-assisted: AI-generated construction (Sandhu, 7 Oct) built on OpenAI's AI result; Thom reworked and checked the proof; GPT Astra helped draft
verification: Unrefereed preprint co-written by a sofic-groups expert (Thom); Douglas–Mghirbi's Lean formalization depends on OpenAI's unrefereed Lean development

problem: Brennan's conjecture (1978) on integrability of |g′|^p for conformal maps; Kraetzer's t²/4 conjecture for the universal integral-means spectrum
result: OpenAI's internal model proved Brennan's conjecture and disproved Kraetzer's conjecture at t = −1 (preprints dated 24 Sept, released 6 Oct). Four experts checked the work and gave a short independent proof that B_b(t) ≤ t²/4 on [−2, 2], strict except at 0 and ±2
human_role: AI-generated original proof; Binder, Ivrii, Prause and Smirnov validated it and wrote a shorter, stronger proof without AI help (some used AI agents to understand the AI proof)
verification: Lean formalization by OpenAI (per its scope note, not independently reviewed) plus an independent expert proof in an unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Gauss circle problem: the exponent θ in E(X) = O(X^θ)
result: θ ≤ 209/670 + ε ≈ 0.31194, improving Li–Yang's 0.314483 and going below Huxley's suggested 5/16 barrier for the Bombieri–Iwaniec method.
human_role: Human-led with AI tools: authors used ChatGPT and Codex to discuss proof strategies and to draft and check parts of the arguments; final proofs written and verified by the authors
verification: Unrefereed preprint; no formal proof

problem: Lonely Runner Conjecture (Wills 1967, Cusick 1973): every runner is at some time at distance ≥ 1/(n+1) from all others
result: ML(V) > (1+c)/(2n) for an absolute constant c > 0, the first constant-factor improvement over the union bound 1/(2n)
human_role: Human-led: authors developed the strategy; ChatGPT 6 Pro/Astra proposed the GCD-sum ingredient, pointed to Green–Walker, fixed gaps and turned informal proofs into rigorous ones
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles (and paths) in an n-vertex tournament: Alon's question (1990) and Wormald's conjecture on the extremal tournament
result: C(n) = (cosh 1/cos 1 ± o(1))(n−1)!/2ⁿ, attained asymptotically by the cyclic regular tournament; asymptotic maximum number of Hamiltonian paths follows
human_role: Authors chose the problem and the strategy hint (permanent estimates); GPT-5.6 found the lower-bound proof and a second instance the upper bound; authors rewrote, simplified and exposited
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; human-written exposition of the AI proofs

problem: Existence of the Smith–Toda complex V(4); V(3) exists for p ≥ 7 (Toda)
result: V(4) exists for every prime p ≥ 11. OpenAI's internal model had shown it only for p = 1009, plus a V(n) at some prime for each n
human_role: OpenAI's model wrote the original papers; Angeltveit checked, simplified and extended them, using ChatGPT as an interactive assistant; he checked all arguments himself
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint by a specialist; OpenAI papers expert-read, no errors found

problem: Lee–Loh–Sudakov conjecture on bipartitions with both directed cuts large; Scott's question on c(d)
result: Sharp bound ⌈(d−1)m/(2(2d−1)) + d²/(2(2d−1))⌉ for every d ≥ 2 and large m, ⌈m/6⌉ for d = 2 and all m, plus stability.
ai_system: Altifina framework; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5
human_role: AI-originated: the core proof (Theorem 1.2) was found by the multi-model framework; Tyomkyn revised and extended it with ChatGPT 6 Astra to the main theorems; humans wrote the paper
verification: Unrefereed preprint; authors state Lean verification (certificate on request, not public)

problem: Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps (Zhitomirskii–Montgomery) in the equiregular case
result: Claimed equiregular rank-two counterexample in dimension 9 whose endpoint map has no regular values.
ai_system: Claude Opus 5; Claude Opus 5.5; Codex; ChatGPT 6 Astra
human_role: AI-assisted: human strategy and line-by-line checking; Claude generated the explicit construction, the moment-problem solution and first proofs; Codex helped with the Lean formalization
verification: Unrefereed preprint; complete Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1–1.3 (author-written statements) on Zenodo

problem: Asymptotic value of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes (Kalai's question)
result: Exact asymptotic rates of the binary and spherical Delsarte LPs for all distances, in closed form via elliptic integrals (matching upper and lower bounds).
ai_system: Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-6 Astra; Codex
human_role: AI-assisted: human-led program; GPT-5.6 Sol co-formulated the upper bounds; Opus 5.5 found the key compatibility and the obstacle-problem reformulation 'with light direction'; Codex drafted
verification: Unrefereed preprint; no formal proof

problem: Hopf's conjecture: even-dimensional manifolds of positive sectional curvature have positive Euler characteristic (symmetric case)
result: Proved for manifolds and orbifolds admitting an effective isometric T³-action (previously T⁴), with the rational cohomology of fixed-point components classified.
human_role: AI-assisted: GPT-6 Astra produced the first proof of Theorem A with minimal human input; the stronger structure theorem, orbifold case and the write-up are human
verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Nienhaus proved the T⁴ case)

problem: Gauss class number problem: list all imaginary quadratic fields of a given class number (effectively, unconditionally)
result: Unconditional determination of all imaginary quadratic fields with class number ≤ 2000 (16,453,493 fields), via an explicit, Lean-verified version of OpenAI's Landau–Siegel zero exclusion.
ai_system: OpenAI internal model (Siegel-zero proof and its Lean formalization); Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code)
human_role: Human-directed: the author chose the problem, checks and trusted base; Claude did constants, Lean, code and most text; the underlying theorem is OpenAI's
verification: Key theorems Lean-verified (two kernels); sieve computation not formally verified; unrefereed preprint; OpenAI's manuscript itself unrefereed

problem: Ghys's conjecture (1995): every holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact complex manifold is conjugate to a holomorphic affine automorphism of a complex infra-nilmanifold
result: Proved in the codimension-one case: such maps are biholomorphically conjugate to hyperbolic automorphisms of a complex torus; this covers complex dimension 3.
human_role: AI-assisted: the author used Intern-S2 in many rounds of dialogue to develop ideas and arguments, then verified everything himself; the Lean formalization was agent-driven (SHEAF) with human checks of the final theorem
verification: Formal proof in Lean (Peking University, SHEAF; repo public); unrefereed arXiv preprint

problem: Hardy–Littlewood–Chowla conjecture, case Σ_{p≤x} µ(p+h) = o(π(x)) (Möbius on shifted primes; parity-problem model case)
result: Claimed: Σ_{p≤x} µ(p+2) = o(π(x)), and each sign of µ(p+2) has density 1/2 among primes with p+2 squarefree
ai_system: ChatGPT; OpenAI internal model (via the OpenAI Math Release preprint)
human_role: Human-written proof; ChatGPT helped the authors understand the OpenAI preprint's method, establish Appendix A and check the manuscript
verification: Unrefereed preprint; no Lean formalization

problem: Erdős–Simonovits rational exponents conjecture (Erdős problem #571): every rational r in [1, 2] is the Turán exponent of some graph
result: Human-written exposition of the AI-found proof: for every rational r in [1, 2] there is a graph H with ex(n, H) = Θ(n^r).
human_role: The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra in Epoch AI's FrontierMath Erdős runs (Sept 2026); eight human experts wrote, explained and situated it in this paper
verification: Lean proof from the Epoch AI run (tadamcz/erdos571) plus an expert-written preprint; not yet refereed

problem: Amenability of Thompson's group F (Thompson 1973; Geoghegan's conjecture)
result: Claimed by OpenAI and re-proved in streamlined form by Kim and Lodha: F is nonamenable.
human_role: Autonomous AI proof (OpenAI release); human experts simplified, generalized and wrote it out without AI
verification: Checked by named independent specialists: Sang-hyun Kim and Yash Lodha give a streamlined proof and a generalisation based on OpenAI's argument, written without AI (arXiv 2610.18360, unrefereed); OpenAI's Lean scope note is unreviewed

problem: Ulam's problem: is every Lie group countably representable (isomorphic to a group of permutations of a countable set)?
result: Yes: every Lie group, and hence every locally compact second countable group, embeds in Sym(N).
human_role: AI-assisted: GPT-6 Astra produced the key countable-index deformation for SL3(R) after three weeks of discussion; the authors extended it to all simple Lie groups, checked it and rewrote the proof
verification: Unrefereed preprint by two established group theorists; no formal proof

problem: Bloch constant conjecture: the Bloch constant equals the Ahlfors–Grunsky value 0.4718616…
result: Disproved: B < A_AG − 1.3 × 10⁻⁹.
human_role: Human-led: proofs developed and written by the author; ChatGPT for exploring approaches and editing; Codex generated the Lean formalization
verification: Lean 4 formalization reported (repository not reachable on 14 Oct); unrefereed preprint

problem: Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of arbitrary number fields
result: For every number field K, ζ_K has no zeros with Re s > 31/32; likewise finite-order Hecke L-functions over K.
human_role: AI-assisted: Cureton and Thorner directed the research and made the mathematical judgments; AxiomProver generated the proofs and the Lean formalization
verification: Formal proof in Lean (public repo); preprint, not peer-reviewed; no independent expert check found yet

problem: Erdős Matching Conjecture (1965); Łuczak–Mieczkowska–Šileikis tail-probability conjecture
result: Tail conjecture proved for all k; Erdős Matching Conjecture proved for fixed k ≥ 3, s sufficiently large, all n ≥ k(s+1).
human_role: AI-assisted: humans built the framework and the k = 2–5 and k ≥ 10^100 cases; AI produced the unified k ≥ 6 argument and the idea that closed a gap
verification: Unrefereed preprint; authors checked AI arguments

problem: Real-rootedness/log-concavity of Chow and chain polynomials of matroids (Ferroni–Schröter, Huh–Stevens, Athanasiadis–Kalampogia-Evangelinou conjectures)
result: Explicit infinite families of matroids whose Chow, augmented Chow, chain and h-polynomials are not log-concave; the real-rootedness conjectures are false.
human_role: AI-assisted search: humans posed the targets and orchestrated LLM searches; models found the counterexample families; humans digested, checked and wrote
verification: Explicit finite counterexamples, checkable by direct computation; unrefereed preprint; no independent check reported

problem: Landau–Siegel zeros (exceptional real zeros of real Dirichlet L-functions)
result: Explicit version of OpenAI's claimed exclusion: (1 − β) log q ≥ 3.0 × 10⁻³ for every primitive real character of conductor q ≥ 3 (with Lu–Zaman–Zhao for small q).
human_role: Expert reconstruction: the proof is OpenAI's; Claude drafted the report, expansion and constants; Banks checked every line
verification: Expert-checked by the author (unrefereed); OpenAI's original has a Lean formalization without explicit constant

problem: Skryabin's conjecture: every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode
result: Proved, in the stronger form: finite uniform dimension on one side implies a bijective antipode.
human_role: AI-assisted: GPT-6 suggested the proof strategy in dialogue; the author developed, checked and wrote the proof
verification: Unrefereed preprint

problem: Vaught's conjecture (1961) for L_ω1,ω: a countable theory/sentence has either countably many or perfectly many (2^ℵ0) countable models
result: Disproved for L_ω1,ω: an explicit sentence with exactly ℵ1 countable models and no perfect set of non-isomorphic models.
ai_system: Claude Code; Codex; Claude Opus 4.5–5.5; Claude Fable 5/5.1; GPT-5.2–GPT-6; GPT Pro
human_role: Human-led: Knight's framework and draft; Ackerman and Freer directed the work; coding agents did the Lean formalization and helped search for the combinatorial template, with SMT/Horn-clause solvers
verification: Formal proof in Lean (Comparator-checked, Palomar Registry); unrefereed preprint

problem: Erdős Problem #1117 / Hayman Problem 2.16: can lim inf ν_f(r) = ∞ for the number of maximum-modulus points of a non-monomial entire function?
result: No: ν_f(r) > 2k only on a locally finite set of radii, with 2k sharp, so lim inf ν_f(r) ≤ 2k.
human_role: AI-assisted: ChatGPT and Codex (GPT-6) 'used to develop the proof and prepare the manuscript'; single human author takes responsibility
verification: Unrefereed preprint (two versions); no formal proof; not yet marked solved on erdosproblems.com

problem: Formal verification of Thurston's geometrization conjecture (posed 1982; proved by Perelman 2003 via Hamilton's Ricci flow)
result: Lean 4 formalization of the geometrization theorem for closed, connected, oriented smooth three-manifolds (prime decomposition, incompressible torus cuts, Thurston-geometric pieces), with no sorry and only the three standard axioms.
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6 Luna; GPT-6 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; Humanize
human_role: Human-led: the authors set the theorem statements and the plan; AI builder agents wrote the Lean code and a GPT-6 Astra reviewer agent checked each round
verification: Formal proof in Lean (kernel-checked, axiom closure reported by the authors); definitions and statement still need independent human review; unrefereed preprint

problem: A Krylov–Safonov Harnack inequality for kinetic equations in nondivergence form with measurable coefficients (missing: an Aleksandrov–Bakelman–Pucci estimate), and Pucci's 1966 conjecture on the optimal integrability exponent in the ABP estimate
result: Aleksandrov estimate sup u ≤ C‖f‖_{L^p} for Kolmogorov equations with rough coefficients, giving the kinetic Krylov–Safonov theorem; AI manuscripts also claim Pucci's conjecture in every dimension and its parabolic version.
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra Ultra; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6 Pro
human_role: Autonomous per the authors: each AI source is marked 'Human contribution: None' (the authors wrote the prompt and research instructions). The six mathematicians checked the kinetic proof, wrote a human exposition and published the chats
verification: Unrefereed preprint: human exposition of the Aleksandrov estimate by six specialists; the Pucci-conjecture manuscripts are AI-generated and their human exposition is still in preparation

problem: Smale's sixth problem: is the number of central configurations (relative equilibria) of the n-body problem finite for every choice of positive masses? Case n = 5 in the plane

human_role: Company says autonomous (no human steering); the paper names no human authors and gives no process details
verification: Lean proof published by the company (not independently built by us); not peer-reviewed; no expert assessment yet

problem: Polynomial Littlewood–Offord problem (Nguyen–Vu conjecture); total influence of bounded-degree rational functions (Kothari–Kovacs-Deak–Wang–Yang conjecture)
result: Optimal anticoncentration bound O_d(r^{-1/2}) for multilinear polynomials of fixed degree, and a total-influence estimate for bounded-degree rational functions.
human_role: Autonomous discovery by GPT-6 Pro per the author; the human verified it and rewrote the argument from scratch
verification: Unrefereed preprint by a specialist in the area; public chat log

problem: Is the rhombicosidodecahedron Rupert? (Steininger–Yurkevich conjecture that it is not; Rupert's question dates to c. 1693)
result: Claimed computer-assisted proof, with interval-arithmetic certificates, that the rhombicosidodecahedron does not have the Rupert property.
human_role: Single teenage author who says he set the topic and direction; Claude generated the proof code and, per one report, helped check it and write the paper
verification: Unverified claim, no expert review: computer-assisted certificates published with code (Zenodo, GitHub); no peer review or independent check reported as of 14 Oct 2026

problem: Linear Hadwiger conjecture (K_t-minor-free graphs have chromatic number O(t))
result: Proved: a universal C with χ(G) ≤ Ct for all K_t-minor-free G
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; OpenAI Codex (6 Sol, Astra)
human_role: AI-generated proof under human direction: authors set the strategy and sub-goals; GPT-6 Astra wrote essentially all of the proof; Codex produced the Lean formalization
verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Norin, Steiner); main theorem formally verified in Lean 4 (no sorries, standard axioms; formal statement written with the authors, not independently audited)

problem: Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture (universal Cheeger/Poincaré constant for isotropic log-concave measures)
result: Universal O(1) bound on the KLS constant ψ_n (Song–Zhang); a second, AI-generated proof via Song–Zhang's criterion (Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec)
ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Fable 5; Claude Fable 5.1; ChatGPT
human_role: AI-assisted (Song–Zhang: human-chosen approaches, AI co-developed); largely AI-generated (Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec: authors mainly understood and exposited ChatGPT's proofs)
verification: Two preprints; expert authors; not peer-reviewed or formalized

problem: ε-Dvoretzky conjecture: polynomial dependence on 1/ε in Dvoretzky's theorem (V. Milman; Klartag–Novikov)
result: Polynomial bound n ≥ (C/ε)^((ℓ+1)/2)|log ε| for nearly ellipsoidal ℓ-dimensional sections of arbitrary (not necessarily symmetric) convex bodies, and a Euclidean-ball version.
human_role: Human-led. The key idea (the probability distribution on the Grassmannian) came out of a discussion between ChatGPT and Shahar Moshe; ChatGPT also checked and improved proofs.
verification: Unrefereed preprint (Tel Aviv University / Weizmann Institute authors)

problem: Six open questions/conjectures incl. Gaussian ellipsoid fitting threshold, biharmonic NLS blow-up (2015), Kida's semiabelian-monomial conjecture (2024)
result: Six papers; Meta says five answer previously open questions (two are conjecture refutations by counterexample; one extends a known connection)
human_role: AI-assisted: mathematicians directed the research; Muse Spark proposed and revised proof strategies, wrote search programs and candidate proofs, and drafted sections that humans verified
verification: Internal review by a second group of mathematicians; papers not yet peer-reviewed

problem: Chromatic number of triangle-free geometric intersection graphs (boxes in R³; Burling 1965) and related girth problems
result: Triangle-free box intersection graphs with χ = (log n)^(1−o(1)), plus girth-g unit-distance, line and circle-tangency constructions.
human_role: AI-found constructions: the author guided ChatGPT Astra (asking for parametric families), then wrote the exposition and analysis
verification: Unrefereed preprint

problem: Lehmer's permutation conjecture (1965): imperfect Hamiltonian traversals of multiset permutations by adjacent swaps; an unsolved research problem in Knuth's TAOCP
result: Proof of Verhoeff's reformulation (Hamiltonicity of the non-stutter-word graph N(S), with two exceptional families), and hence of Lehmer's conjecture.
human_role: Human-led long project; the final short proof was found and developed by Claude Opus 5.5 in a multi-agent setup, then re-derived and checked by the author
verification: Lean formalization by Harmonic's Aristotle (per the paper); unrefereed preprint

problem: Tammes problem for 15 points (open since Tammes 1930; solved for N ≤ 14 and N = 24); Robbins' problem (is V > 2?, Bruss–Ferguson 1996); Hoffman–Johnson–Junge frog-model conjecture for d = 3, 4 (2017)
result: Tammes optimum for N = 15 determined, with exactly two optimal configurations; V > 2 for Robbins' problem; frog model recurrent on the 3-ary and transient on the 4-ary tree; plus three smaller conjectures settled.
human_role: Claimed fully AI-generated ('results, proofs and code were found and written by AI'); the human operator is anonymous. One Tammes theorem came from a third party using Claude
verification: Unverified claim, no expert review (anonymous author): Lean 4 with Mathlib (standard axioms, comparator-checked); Tammes leaves graph enumeration and program correctness as explicit hypotheses backed by replayed certificates; unrefereed Zenodo preprints

problem: Barvinok's log-concavity conjecture for contingency-table counts (line version); Ferroni–Higashitani conjecture on Ehrhart polynomial evaluations
result: Log-concavity on lines for lattice-point counts of unimodular polytopes, a lower bound for all TU polytopes and a deterministic approximate-counting algorithm.
human_role: Key theorem proven by ChatGPT 6 Astra; authors generalised it (following an AI-suggested remark), verified everything and wrote the paper
verification: Unrefereed preprint

problem: List Total Colouring Conjecture (Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall; Juvan–Mohar–Škrekovski; Hilton–Johnson)
result: Disproved: an explicit 20-vertex cubic graph with total chromatic number 4 and list total chromatic number 5.

verification: Unrefereed preprint; short explicit proof checked by the author

problem: Lovász conjecture (1969): every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path; quantitative version, the longest guaranteed cycle
result: Every connected vertex-transitive graph on n vertices contains a cycle of length n^(1−o(1)), up from n^(2/3−o(1)).
human_role: Human-led with substantive AI input: the authors' framework; GPT-5.6 Sol found two key literature tools and supplied the group-theoretic Lemma 6.1
verification: Unrefereed preprint

result: Claimed: exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration for every four positive masses and every cyclic ordering.
human_role: AI-generated per the author's disclosure (AI found and proved the results, wrote the programs, the Lean formalization and the draft); the human role is not described
verification: Unverified claim, no expert review: unrefereed preprint by an independent researcher; Lean formalization reported (Lean kernel and nanoda), formal statement not audited by others; computation repeated with a second program

problem: Schiffer and Pompeiu conjectures in dimensions n ≥ 3 and for convex domains
result: Bounded convex non-ball domains with real-analytic spherical boundary in dimensions 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14 that admit a nonconstant solution of Δu + u = 0 with u = 1 and ∇u = 0 on the boundary, so both conjectures fail there, even for convex domains.
ai_system: Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6 Sol
human_role: Single author; AI assistance disclosed without detail on its extent
verification: Computer-assisted proof with public certificates; preprint, not peer-reviewed

problem: Erdős Problem #993 (Alavi, Malde, Schwenk, Erdős 1987): is the independent set sequence of every tree or forest unimodal?
result: Claimed: yes for every finite forest. Two proofs: Zhang–Li (27 Sept 2026, computer-assisted, GPT-6 Astra for computations) and Li–Vallier–Zhang (6 Oct 2026, new arguments and Lean 4 proof attributed to AI agents).
ai_system: Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Fable 5.1; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-6 Sol; GPT-6.1 Sol

problem: Zarankiewicz problem at density 1/2 and diagonal bipartite Ramsey numbers b(t,t)
result: b(t,t) = O(2^t); K_{t,t} guaranteed in balanced bipartite graphs of density 1/2 once N ≥ c·2^t.
human_role: AI-found proof after guided prompting; human rewrote and takes responsibility
verification: Unrefereed preprint

problem: Erdős problems #18(b), #859, #1062(ii) and Ben Green's open problems 24, 39, 40, as formalised on Conjectures.io
result: Lean 4 proofs accepted and paid by Conjectures.io; see key facts for each statement

verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (no sorry, standard axioms only); not peer-reviewed

verification: Formal proof in Lean 4, plus expert check; preprint, not peer-reviewed

problem: Courtade–Kumar (most informative Boolean function) conjecture: dictators maximise I(f(X); Y) under binary symmetric noise
result: Proved in full (all n, all noise levels, no balance assumption) by three independent teams on 21–22 Sep 2026; the Google–CUHK proof is computer-assisted and verified end-to-end in Lean.

human_role: Google–CUHK: humans supplied the reduction and the Bellman function, AI generated most new ideas and the region-by-region proof; Ky–Tran: human approach, ChatGPT developed the proofs; Mahdavifar–Beirami: AI generated the single-bit proof under human direction

problem: Irrationality of ζ(5) = Σ 1/n⁵ (open since Apéry's 1978 proof for ζ(3); Euler-era question)
result: ζ(5) is irrational, with integer polynomials Q_n of degree 37n satisfying 0 < Q_n(ζ(5)) < exp(−139n²/5), and irrationality measure at most 260.

verification: Formal proof in Lean (Codex-generated formalization of the Chang–Liu–Liu proof); preprints not yet refereed

problem: Goldbach-type problem for the Liouville function (Shusterman's question)

human_role: Unknown; pseudonymous release with no first-party account of AI use

problem: Erdős problem #108: Erdős–Hajnal high-girth, high-chromatic subgraph problem

problem: Sylvester's conjecture (1879): every prime p ≡ 4, 7, 8 (mod 9) is a sum of two rational cubes
result: Proved in full: the 4, 7 cases by Yin (arXiv 2605.25917, May 2026), the 8 case by Burungale–Tian (arXiv 2609.14893, Sept 2026), who show E_p: y² = x³ + p²/4 has analytic rank one; a shorter proof of the 8 case followed from Yin (arXiv 2610.08015, Oct 2026).

problem: Sendov's conjecture
result: Proof of Sendov's conjecture for all degrees, formally verified in Lean.
human_role: Human orchestrated (Mazur); Tao simplified and formalised with AI agents
verification: Formal proof in Lean; expert-checked by Tao

problem: Heil–Ramanathan–Topiwala (HRT) conjecture on linear independence of time-frequency shifts
result: Explicit counterexample: 12 time-frequency shifts of a Schwartz function are linearly dependent, disproving the HRT conjecture.
human_role: Human-led with AI assistance for strategy and parameter search; humans wrote and checked the proof
verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Faulhuber, Petersen, van Velthoven, Voigtlaender) with certified numerics; v2 adds a purely analytic proof of a qualitative counterexample; Terence Tao posted a partial digestion; not formalised in Lean

problem: Period-index conjecture
result: Varieties of every dimension d ≥ 3 with a Brauer class of period 2 and index 2^d, contradicting the conjecture; a corrected conjecture is proposed.
human_role: Human-led: a wrong AI example inspired the construction; the human found and proved the correct one, with AI help on literature search and lattice calculations
verification: Preprint by an expert in the field; not peer-reviewed

problem: Schiffer's conjecture (Yau Problem 80) and the planar Pompeiu problem
result: Non-circular bounded planar domains carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction that is constant on the boundary, which disproves both Schiffer's conjecture and the Pompeiu conjecture in the plane (one explicit domain, and an infinite family).
ai_system: GPT-5.6; GPT-5.5; Claude Opus 4.8; Claude Fable 5; ChatGPT/Codex
human_role: Human-led. Colbrook–Stepaniants: AI only helped debug code. Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont: humans devised the bifurcation strategy; LLMs checked estimates numerically and drafted some lemma proofs, and GPT-5.6 wrote the Lean formalisation
verification: Computer-assisted interval certificate (Colbrook–Stepaniants); Lean 4 formalisation (Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont); not yet peer-reviewed

problem: Ten open problems incl. existence of explicit non-sofic groups, Connes rigidity, Erdős #146/#180/#183, sphere-packing bounds
result: Claimed resolutions or improvements on ten open problems, most with Lean-formalised proofs.
human_role: Largely autonomous per OpenAI; humans selected problems and checked
verification: Lean 4 formalizations published for most of the ten results (openai/ten-proofs); results not refereed; a review of 18 chapter reviews (Sienicki & Sienicki, arXiv 2608.14673, unrefereed) found no remaining substantive error in principal results but one chapter needing major revision; experts disputed attribution and citation (Scientific American). Status varies by result

problem: Crouzeix's conjecture
result: Proof that the numerical range W(A) is a 2-spectral set for every matrix A.
human_role: Autonomous: non-specialist prompted; experts verified
verification: Expert-checked (Crouzeix, Greenbaum, Townsend); preprint

problem: Optimal universal constant in the thin-shell (variance) theorem for isotropic log-concave distributions
result: Var(|X|²) ≤ 8n for every isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n, sharp for i.i.d. centered exponential coordinates; among uniform distributions on convex bodies the regular simplex is extremal.
human_role: Human prompts and direction (Chen, after discussions with Klartag); the model produced the initial proof; both authors verified, revised and rewrote it
verification: Unrefereed preprint; proof verified and rewritten by the two authors, both specialists in the field; chat log published with the paper

problem: Hessian conjecture: a polynomial whose Hessian determinant is a nonzero constant has an injective gradient map
result: Counterexample for n=5 (hence all n≥5); status now: true for n≤3, false for n≥5, open for n=4
ai_system: Claude Fable 5 (indirectly, via the Jacobian counterexample)
human_role: Human-led; built by hand on an AI-assisted result
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2607.22198); explicit counterexample, checkable by computation; the paper reports no AI use

problem: Rota's unimodality conjecture for the number of flats of a matroid by rank (and Mason's log-concavity conjecture)
result: Explicit matroids whose flat counts are not unimodal (Rota), not log-concave (Mason), and can have arbitrarily many peaks.
ai_system: ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; Claude Opus 4.8
human_role: AI-assisted: humans directed the search and wrote the papers; ChatGPT found initial counterexamples/constructions that the authors generalized
verification: Explicit, checkable counterexamples in arXiv preprints; not yet peer-reviewed

problem: Dinitz–Garg–Goemans (Goemans) conjecture on the cost of unsplittable flows
result: Claimed counterexample: a small single-source, three-terminal instance with fractional flow cost 58 where every unsplittable flow with capacity violation ≤ 15 costs at least 60.
human_role: Rybin prompted GPT-5.6 Pro with a few short prompts; the model found the instance; Rybin published the chat
verification: Unverified claim (X post with chat log); arithmetic reportedly checked by others; no paper or peer review found

problem: Six open problems from the Erdős problems collection (numbers not identified)
result: Claimed solutions to six open Erdős problems in five days out of about 13 attempted.
human_role: Wang chose problems, wrote the prompts and acceptance criteria and audited outputs; GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex did the long searches and drafts
verification: Unverified claim (X thread); no database update or expert check found

problem: Jacobian conjecture (Keller 1939): a polynomial map with non-zero constant Jacobian determinant is invertible
result: Explicit non-injective polynomial map C³→C³ with constant Jacobian determinant, disproving the conjecture for all n≥3.
human_role: AI-assisted: human chose the problem and verified; Claude found the counterexample
verification: Explicit map, checkable by direct computation (constant Jacobian determinant and three points with the same image); digested and generalised by Terence Tao, Gallagher, Speyer and Shuhong Gao; no refereed paper by the discoverers

problem: Cycle double cover conjecture
result: Proof that every bridgeless graph admits a cycle double cover.
human_role: Autonomous proof per OpenAI; human experts wrote independent expositions
verification: Checked by independent graph theorists: Jim Geelen (notes, arXiv 2607.15399) and Sang-il Oum (exposition, arXiv 2607.16356); OpenAI's proof is a PDF, not refereed; a Lean formalisation is reported but not verified here

problem: Query complexity of derivative-free (zeroth-order, exact-value) convex Lipschitz optimization: gap between Protasov's ~d² upper bound and the ~d lower bound
result: Deterministic lower bound Ω(d²/log(d+1)), matching Protasov's 1996 upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors.
human_role: AI-assisted: the researcher wrote a 10-page guiding prompt after a year on the problem; the model produced the proof; the human wrote the paper and checked it in Lean
verification: Partial Lean: the core deterministic lower bound is formally verified in Lean 4 (public repo); the upper-bound and transfer results are not formalized; unrefereed single-author preprint

problem: Grothendieck's question: is every finite locally free group scheme of order n killed by n?
result: A counterexample of order 4 not killed by 4, over a non-reduced base.
human_role: AI-assisted: Akhil Mathew directed the search and verified
verification: Formal proof in Lean (Mathlib)

problem: Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture (over R)
result: Finite sets of reals with both sumset and product set of size at most |A|^(2−c), disproving the conjecture over R; later reproduced autonomously by an AI agent.
human_role: Original disproof human-led, inspired by an AI result; follow-up shows autonomous AI rediscovery
verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, Zhelezov, arXiv 2605.28781); the autonomous AI rediscovery is a separate unrefereed preprint (Huang, arXiv 2607.20525); no formal proof

problem: Erdős unit distance conjecture (planar point sets: at most N^(1+o(1)) unit distances)
result: Construction of planar N-point sets with at least N^(1+δ) unit distances for a fixed tiny δ>0, disproving Erdős's conjectured upper bound, via algebraic number theory; humans improved the exponent within weeks.
human_role: Autonomous discovery by the model; checked and refined by human mathematicians
verification: Expert-checked (Timothy Gowers and others); human follow-up papers

problem: McKean's conjecture on entropy along the heat flow; Gaussian completely monotone (GCM) conjecture
result: Explicit measure on R with positive 5th derivative of entropy under heat flow, refuting three related conjectures.
human_role: AI found the counterexample; humans verified and wrote the proof
verification: Unrefereed preprint (Gu & Sellke, arXiv 2605.11656) with a human-written proof; the multidimensional disproof by Zou, Fan, Gao and Wang (arXiv 2605.18081) is also an unrefereed preprint; no formal proof

problem: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.10; FrontierMath Tier 4
result: Resolution of a Kourovka Notebook group-theory problem with a human mathematician; state-of-the-art 48% on FrontierMath Tier 4.
human_role: Human-led with AI tools (Lackenby); benchmark autonomous
verification: Unrefereed preprint (arXiv 2605.06651); results checked by the collaborating mathematicians (e.g. Marc Lackenby), no independent check

problem: Erdős problem #1196 (Erdős–Sárközy–Szemerédi conjectures on primitive sets)
result: Proof of the conjectured bounds for primitive sets and divisibility chains, plus a new short proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture.
human_role: AI-generated key idea from a non-expert's prompt; professional mathematicians verified and wrote the paper
verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2605.00301) by eight authors including the specialists Jared Duker Lichtman and Terence Tao (both co-authors, so not independent checks); no formal proof

problem: Borsuk's conjecture: smallest dimension where it fails
result: Counterexample in dimension 63 (321-point three-distance set needing ≥ 65 parts), improving the 2013 record of 64.
human_role: AI-assisted: Max Grinsztajn worked with GPT-5.5 Pro; exact computer verification
verification: Explicit finite construction with an exact verification script and Sage-checkable certificates (no Lean); listed in Tao's optimization-constants repository; not peer-reviewed

problem: Erdős Problem #650: how many integers of a set A can always be matched to distinct multiples inside an interval of length 2·max(A)
result: f(m) = min(m, ⌈2√m⌉) for all m, settling the problem exactly
human_role: AI-assisted: ChatGPT proposed the strategy, Aristotle produced the Lean-verified argument; the authors simplified it and wrote the paper
verification: Formal proof in Lean by Aristotle (per the authors); human-written exposition in an unrefereed arXiv preprint; erdosproblems.com lists the problem as solved

problem: Lower bounds for classical two-colour Ramsey numbers R(3,k), R(4,k)
result: Explicit colourings improving nine long-studied Ramsey lower bounds.
human_role: Humans set up search and scoring; constructions found by AI
verification: Explicit constructions checkable by computer; arXiv preprint

problem: Formal verification of optimal sphere packing in dimensions 8 and 24 (Viazovska 2016; Cohn–Kumar–Miller–Radchenko–Viazovska 2017)
result: Complete Lean formalisations of both theorems, correcting minor errors in the published proofs.
human_role: AI-assisted: agent built on a human-started blueprint project
verification: Formal proof in Lean

problem: Decomposing the 3D torus digraph on m³ vertices into three Hamiltonian cycles
result: General explicit construction for all odd m, found by Claude and proved by Knuth.
human_role: AI-assisted: colleague Filip Stappers ran the Claude session; Knuth verified and proved
verification: Human proof by Knuth; formalised in Lean

problem: Open Erdős problems; conjecture in online optimisation; cosmic-string radiation calculations
result: Several Erdős problems solved autonomously, a decade-old online-optimisation conjecture refuted, and a new analytic technique for cosmic-string radiation.
human_role: Mixed: some autonomous; others in collaboration with 18 external researchers
verification: Batch of results in unrefereed preprints (arXiv 2602.10177 and companion papers), checked by the collaborating mathematicians, who are co-authors; one generalisation reported as peer-reviewed (not verified here). Status varies by result

problem: Erdős problem #728
result: Full solution of the intended version of #728, generated by GPT-5.2 Pro and machine-checked in Lean by Aristotle.
human_role: Near-autonomous: human relayed prompts between two AI systems
verification: Formal proof in Lean; endorsed by Terence Tao

problem: Erdős problems #124, #367, #707, #1026 and others
result: First AI-involved genuine new solutions of listed-open Erdős problems, including a full solution of #1026 and a Lean-verified autonomous proof for a variant of #124.
ai_system: Aristotle; AlphaEvolve; Gemini Deep Think; GPT-5
human_role: Mixed: #124 near-autonomous (formal statement given); #1026 human–AI collaboration
verification: Formal proofs in Lean for key steps; expert-checked (Tao, Bloom)

problem: Broad battery of optimisation-type open problems (e.g. inequalities, packings, finite-field Kakeya-type constructions)
result: Systematic evidence that LLM-driven evolutionary search matches or beats best-known constructions across dozens of problems.
human_role: Human-led with AI tools: mathematicians chose problems and scorers
verification: Explicit constructions checkable by computation (problem repository public); unrefereed arXiv preprint (2511.02864)

problem: Problems listed as 'open' on erdosproblems.com
result: No new mathematics: GPT-5 located existing published solutions to about 10 listed problems and partial results on 11 others.
human_role: Human researchers prompted literature search and publicised results
verification: Checked by Thomas Bloom (site maintainer)

problem: Finite-time singularity formation in fluid equations (Euler, Boussinesq, IPM)
result: Discovery of previously unknown families of unstable self-similar blow-up solutions, computed to near machine precision.
ai_system: physics-informed neural networks with Gauss–Newton optimisation
human_role: Human-led with AI tools: co-designed by mathematicians
verification: Numerical: high-precision computation of unstable self-similar profiles, not a computer-assisted proof; unrefereed arXiv preprint (2509.14185)

problem: Formalising the strong Prime Number Theorem (with error term) in Lean
result: Complete machine-checked formalisation produced largely by an AI agent in 3 weeks.
human_role: AI-assisted: agent wrote most Lean code from the human blueprint; humans supervised
verification: Formal proof in Lean (compiles against Mathlib)

problem: Convexity of the gradient-descent optimisation curve for L-smooth convex functions
result: A correct, novel proof of the bound η ≤ 1.5/L, improving v1's 1/L but weaker than the humans' tight 1.75/L result already posted.
human_role: Human posed the problem and verified the proof
verification: Informal proof checked by Sébastien Bubeck (OpenAI), who posed the question; not written up as a paper or refereed; the human authors' revised paper already had the tight 1.75/L bound

problem: 4×4 complex matrix multiplication (Strassen 1969: 49 multiplications); kissing number in 11 dimensions; ~50 open problems
result: 48 scalar multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices; kissing configuration of 593 spheres in 11D (previous 592); matched SOTA on ~75% and improved ~20% of 50+ problems.
human_role: Humans define the problem and an automated scorer; evolutionary LLM search autonomous
verification: Constructions verified computationally (independent GitHub checks); white paper, later arXiv

problem: Olympiad-level geometry proofs
result: 25 of 30 IMO geometry problems solved with human-readable proofs.
human_role: Autonomous
verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; proofs checked by an IMO coach (Evan Chen)

problem: Cap set problem: largest subsets of F_3^n with no three points on a line
result: Largest known cap set in dimension 8 (512 vs 496) and improved capacity lower bound.
human_role: Humans wrote program skeleton and evaluator; LLM-driven search autonomous
verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; constructions verified computationally

problem: Combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials; relations between knot invariants
result: ML-guided discovery of a conjectured, then proved, relation between the knot signature and hyperbolic invariants, and a new approach to combinatorial invariance for symmetric groups.
ai_system: supervised neural networks with gradient saliency
human_role: Human-led with AI tools: ML suggested patterns; mathematicians formulated and proved the theorems
verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; human proofs

problem: Several published conjectures on graph invariants
result: Explicit counterexamples found by an RL agent that treats building a graph as a game, rewarded by how badly the conjecture fails.
human_role: Human chose conjectures and reward functions; search autonomous; counterexamples trivially checkable
verification: Counterexamples checkable by direct computation; reimplemented by others (arXiv 2403.18429)
